key_insight: The paper turns difficult Gaussian entanglement and communication bounds into a convex-geometric optimization problem with provable convergence and polynomial-time accuracy guarantees for fixed rational covariance inputs.
engineering_relevance: It provides computable upper bounds on entanglement, secret key, and two-way assisted quantum/private communication rates for lossy, noisy continuous-variable links, useful for evaluating photonic quantum network designs.
method: Defines Gaussian-restricted relative entropy of entanglement and Rains entanglement via an integral representation and matrix geometric means.
Uses convex-majorization optimization to find unique optimal Gaussian reference states and prove additivity for independent Gaussian inputs.
Extends the framework with teleportation simulation, passive-basis loss optimization, and photon-number truncation for unrestricted quantities.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit convergence rates, bit-complexity bounds, and numerical two- and three-mode examples that match or compare against known pure-loss benchmarks.
watch_item: The strongest complexity guarantees apply to fixed rational input covariance matrices, so practical implementation still depends on accurate numerical integration, subproblem solving, and energy/truncation choices.
paper_title: Gaussian entanglement and quantum communication: geodesic optimization and multimode bounds
